_comment: The permission boundary. Data, not code, so it can be audited and diffed
without reading Python. D.O. may read this file; it may never write it.
First matching rule wins, so order is meaningful. Default is deny.

rules.note: name resolution only; no payload leaves the host
TCP reachability probe; connect then close, no data sent
retrieving a page is an outward-facing action with a remote log entry
local inference costs RAM and nothing else; no data leaves the host
remote inference spends the creator's money and sends state off-host
writes are confined to var/sandbox by realpath prefix check
reads outside the sandbox are not permitted in v1
writes outside the sandbox are never allowed in v1
housekeeping inside D.O.'s own footprint; every action is regenerable, derived from the ledger, or compressed in place - none are irreversible
housekeeping is scoped to own:<action>; there is no path to the creator's files
there is no general delete effect; removal happens only inside declared housekeeping actions
arbitrary subprocess execution is disabled in v1; there is no autonomous path to code execution
the host's own synthesiser: no account, no cost, and nothing leaves the machine
speaking to the creator on their own machine, with a metered budget; the text is one cognition already produced and this cannot change it
asking the creator is the cheapest legitimate way to reduce uncertainty
